headline: SMASH TV lands exposed — the arcade's no-mercy law ships
lede: Williams 1990 never shielded the contestant, and now the arena doesn't either: room entries and respawns land unshielded, and the autopilot still clears all nine seeds by reading the throw instead of tanking it.

notes.text: #2491: the spawn shields (70 ticks on room entry, 150 after death) are gone from SMASH TV — the last softener vs the cabinet, removed. The pilot learned four laws in exchange: lane-sound duel (never align onto a lane chrome owns), spawn-lean parking (read the queue, never loiter a landing ring), dry-tank reload (a LASER at 0 energy is silence — go refill), and open-door landing (never respawn into a body parked on the spawn cell).

Honest re-measure: solo sweep 9/9 unshielded, co-op 9/9, slack seeds 0-2 all win, and the deathless matinee moved from {1,5,7} to {7,8} — under zero mercy the opening volley costs first blood on seven boards, exactly like the arcade.

The proof can fail: smashcheck PASS 766 with --mutate PASS 817 — seven new mutants (four mercyBack variants: any shield creeping back onto a spawn dies; three doctrine erasers) all die, plus smashplay 42/42 in live Chrome watching a respawn meet a round and pay for it with zero page errors.

QA polish filed (#2507): can a phone-thumb read the opening volley at 1x? Respawn-danger telegraphy, low-POWER legibility, and the one honest framing gap left (mild cabinet entry scale) are the next round.

look.text: SMASH TV — take the show unshielded: tap, read the fan, pay nothing for it
